title: `round`, `floor`, `ceil`, `atan2`, `sqrt` and `power` on FLOAT and DOUBLE: zero signs, types and `power(1, ±inf)`
verdict: as the profile: `round_zero_sign` = `IEEE`, `zero_sign` = `IEEE`, `pow_one_inf` = `ONE`; no integer conversion (`float_to_int` does not arise)
description: `round`, `ceil` and `floor` return the argument's own type, DOUBLE for DOUBLE and FLOAT for FLOAT, never an integer: `float_to_int` does not arise for them (past 2^63 the value stays a float: `round(1e30)` is 1e30). A negative value that reaches zero gives `-0.0` (`round(-0.4)`, `ceil(-0.4)`, `ceil(-0.6)`), and `-0.0` stays `-0.0` through all three, for FLOAT as for DOUBLE. NaN and ±inf come back unchanged.

`atan2` and `sqrt` keep the sign of a zero argument: `atan2(-0.0, 1)` and `sqrt(-0.0)` are `-0.0`, `atan2(0.0, -1)` is π and `atan2(±0.0, -0.0)` is -π. `atan2` of FLOATs is typed DOUBLE (the arguments are cast); `sqrt` and `power` of FLOATs likewise give DOUBLE.
`power(1, ±inf)`, `power(-1, ±inf)`, `power(1, NaN)` and `power(NaN, 0)` are 1.0 on FLOAT arguments, as on DOUBLE (duckdb-pow-one-inf).
reference: The sign of a zero result of `round`, `floor` and `ceil` is `round_zero_sign`, left open by the reference (`eval` gives `+0.0`; the ruling of 2026-11-09 in duckdb-R15-round); `zero_sign` = `ONE_ZERO`; `pow_one_inf` = `ONE` (D40). `round`, `floor` and `ceil` return the double, so `float_to_int` does not arise.

evidence.sql: SELECT typeof(round(x)), round(x), ceil(x), floor(x) FROM (VALUES (-0.4::DOUBLE),(-0.6::DOUBLE),(0.4::DOUBLE),(-0.0::DOUBLE)) t(x)
SELECT typeof(round(x)), round(x), ceil(x), floor(x) FROM (VALUES (-0.4::FLOAT),(-0.6::FLOAT),(0.4::FLOAT),(-0.0::FLOAT)) t(x)
SELECT round(x), ceil(x), floor(x) FROM (VALUES (1e30::DOUBLE),('inf'::DOUBLE),('-inf'::DOUBLE),('nan'::DOUBLE)) t(x)
evidence.observed: 1e30 1e30 1e30; inf inf inf; -inf -inf -inf; nan nan nan (FLOAT the same, 1e30 as 1.0000000150474662e+30)

evidence.sql: SELECT atan2(y,x), signbit(atan2(y,x)), sqrt(y), signbit(sqrt(y)), typeof(atan2(y,x)) FROM (VALUES (-0.0::FLOAT,1.0::FLOAT),(-0.0::FLOAT,-1.0::FLOAT),(0.0::FLOAT,-1.0::FLOAT),(-0.0::FLOAT,-0.0::FLOAT)) t(y,x)
evidence.observed: (-0.0, true, -0.0, true, DOUBLE), (-3.141592653589793, true, -0.0, true), (3.141592653589793, false, 0.0, false), (-3.141592653589793, true, -0.0, true); the DOUBLE case gives the same
